author: NorthEast News Desk
body: More than 3,000 athletes from over 100 countries took part in the sixth World Nomad Games in Kyrgyzstan, organizers said. The biennial competition returned to the country where it began in 2014, using traditional sports to combine international competition with Central Asian culture.

Events included horseback archery, several wrestling styles, falconry, tug of war and traditional board games. The program also featured kok boru, a mounted team sport often compared with polo but played with a sheep carcass instead of a ball.

Among the Western participants was British horseback archer Becca Sweetman, who has competed for Great Britain after taking up the sport eight years ago. A British tug-of-war group also traveled to the event, reflecting the games’ widening reach beyond countries where nomadic competitions remain part of everyday sporting culture.

The setting in the mountainous Issyk-Kul region is central to the event’s identity, not merely a backdrop. By drawing competitors who learned the disciplines abroad, the games are developing into both a cultural showcase and a serious international meet. Their growth also offers lesser-known sports a rare stage alongside the global calendar’s established competitions.
dek: The biennial event brought participants from more than 100 countries together for horse archery, wrestling, falconry and traditional games.
headline: Western athletes join 3,000 competitors at Kyrgyzstan’s Nomad Games
